subject: Request: Exceptional hosted API concession for HelioHealth (30% for 12 months)
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FYI — HelioHealth asking for 30% discount to stay (call notes + forecast)

Neha —

Quick recap from this morning's call with Jordan (Head of Data at HelioHealth): they are in the middle of a procurement review led by their CFO and have a competing vendor offering a 25% blended rate if they consolidate. Helio is very pleased with our latency and quality but the sticking point is unit economics for the next 12 months.

They asked if we can do a 30% off hosted API list rate for a committed 12-month term to keep them from moving. Jordan shared a 12-month usage forecast (attached) that shows a front-loaded ramp into Q1 next year (they expect sustained volume).

Why I think it's strategic:
- They are a large payer-network (mid-sized national) — strong reference value in healthcare vertical.
- They want private deployment later (potential Redwood Private upsell).
- Competitive risk: losing them increases churn risk in the vertical and could drive narrative to move to competitor.

Requested next step: need exec-level pricing authorization for >20% concession (they asked 30%). I recommend we table a timeboxed 30% off hosted API list for 12 months with an agreed SLO and a 150% overage true-up clause if usage exceeds forecast by >40%.

Attachments: Helio_2027_usage_forecast.xlsx

Ben
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

- Potential to convert to Private in 12–18 months (upsell motion).

Please evaluate financial impact and legal implications. I'm requesting exec approval to grant an initial 30% off list for 12 months with the guardrails above, contingent on legal-approved SOW.

If this needs Marcus' signoff, please route to him with recommended memo.

2) Signoff on the proposed true-up (150% overage price) and requirement for a minimum commit (we should require a revenue floor to protect economics).

I've drafted an approval memo and attached a redlined SOW that includes the true-up and minimum commit language. Legal needs to review the redline before finalization.

I reviewed the memo and supporting forecast. I'm authorizing a one-time 30% concession for the 12-month committed term for HelioHealth (deal HL-3472) under the following conditions:

1) Must include a minimum revenue floor of $225,000 for the 12-month period (if actual billings fall below this, Helio will owe the difference).

5) This concession is limited to hosted API usage only and excludes any Private deployment credits.

I expect Deal Desk to document the business case in our concessions log and track any downstream upsell activity. Please proceed.
